(8 goals) | matches = 240 | total goals = 569 | average attendance = 7,416 {{cite web|url=http://stats.football365.co.za/dom/SAF/PR/attend.html|title=SA Premiership 2008–2009 Season Attendance Table|date=26 May 2009|publisher=football365.co.za|access-date=29 March 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071128073829/http://stats.football365.co.za/dom/SAF/PR/attend.html|archive-date=28 November 2007|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} | prevseason = [[2007–08 South African Premiership|2007–08]] | nextseason = [[2009–10 Premier Soccer League|2009–10]] }} The '''2008–09 South African Premiership''', known as the '''ABSA Premiership''' for sponsorship purposes, and also commonly referred to as the [[Premier Soccer League|PSL]] after the governing body, was the thirteenth season of the [[South African Premiership|Premiership]] since its establishment in 1996. [[Supersport United]] were the defending champions, having won their first Premiership title on the final day of the previous season. The campaign began in August 2008, ended in May 2009. A total of 16 teams contested in the league, 14 of which contested in the 2007–08 season, and two of which were promoted from the [[National First Division]]. ==Season summary== [[SuperSport United]] defended their title to win their second consecutive Premiership title. [[Orlando Pirates]] came close to taking the title in the final two games. Having drawn their penultimate game 1–1 against SuperSport, it went into the final game with SuperSport on 54 points - sitting two points clear with a superior goal difference. Pirates won their game against [[Amazulu]] 3–1, while SuperSport and [[Santos F.C. (South Africa)|Santos]] played out a goalless draw. Both teams were tied at the top of the points table with 55 points each. [[SuperSport United]] won the league due to a greater goal difference, with +23 goals over [[Orlando Pirates]]'s +17 goals. [[Bay United]] were relegated to the [[National First Division|National League]] after finishing at the bottom of the table on 21 points. [[Thanda Royal Zulu]] entered a playoff with teams from the [[National First Division|National League]] to determine if they would retain their place in the Premiership or be relegated to the [[National First Division|National League]] after ending 15th on the league table with 33 points. [[Bloemfontein Celtic]] survived relegation on goal difference, ending 14th on the league table with 33 points. They were tied with [[Thanda Royal Zulu]], but their goal difference were greater than that of [[Thanda Royal Zulu]]. ==Clubs== {{colbegin|colwidth=18em}} *[[Ajax Cape Town]] *[[AmaZulu F.C. It was the second time that the [[Orlando Pirates]] midfielder bagged the coveted Footballer of the Year honour, following his controversial win last season. This time, however, Modise's brilliance from the unusual left of midfield position helped Pirates mount a championship bid. [[Lucas Thwala]], who earlier this month was named Pirates' Player of the Season ahead of Modise, was named the Premiership Player of the Year.
